summary: A scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology, Qian Lin studied at Fudan University, the University of Bristol (MA), and the University of Washington (PhD), supervised by Collett Cox and Richard G. Salomon. She was attested at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem in 2026.

A scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Ning completed master's degrees at UCAS and the University of Warwick, studying under Hung Wu and Irene Winter. He held teaching posts at Michigan, Yale, and San Diego State, and researched at Dunhuang Academy.

A scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies, Liang studied at Xuehai Tang and under Youwei Kang (~1890–1898). He headed the Translation Bureau (1898) and the National Library of China (~1925–1927), and taught at Current Affairs Academy, Nankai, and Tsinghua.

Duan (1953–2022) specialized in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied at Peking University under Ji Xianlin and Jiang Zhongxin, and earned her PhD at the University of Hamburg under Ronald Emmerick, later serving as professor at Peking University (~1987–2022).

A scholar of Tibetology and history, Chen studied at Qinghai Nationalities University and Minzu University of China under Wang Yao. He taught at Qinghai Nationalities University, Minzu University, and Southwest Minzu University, later directing the Historical Research Institute at the China Tibetology Research Center.

A specialist in linguistics, Buddhist studies, and Sinology, Zhu earned degrees from Northwest Normal University, Central China Normal University, and Sichuan University (PhD 2000). He held professorships at Peking University (1998–2014) and the Education University of Hong Kong (attested 2010).
A Buddhist studies scholar, Qinni Liu studied at Fo Guang University, earning a Master of Arts under the supervision of Kirill Solonin.
A Buddhist studies scholar, Qiwen Xiao studied at Fo Guang University, completing a Master of Arts under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2013).

Devers works in history, archaeology, and Tibetology. He served as a research assistant at the University of Virginia (2008–2010), an archaeologist at Heritage WA (2012), and became a chargé de recherche at the CNRS in 2016.

R. Balasubramanian (1929–2017) was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under the traditional teacher Varahur Kalyanasundara Sastri. He served as Director at the University of Madras from circa 1978 to 1990.

R. D. Vadekar (1902–1986) was a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies who studied under Shripad Krishna Belvalkar. He served as Professor of Sanskrit and Allied Languages at Fergusson College (attested 1958).
A scholar in Indology, R. Gayathri pursued doctoral research at the Kuppuswami Sastri Research Institute under the supervision of V. Yamuna Devi (attested 2026).

Wasson (1898–1986) worked in religious studies and Indology. Educated at Columbia and the LSE, he worked in journalism, joined J.P. Morgan & Co. (1934–1963), and served on the ACLS Executive Committee (1951).

R. H. Blyth (1898–1964) was a scholar in Japanology and Buddhist studies who studied at the University of London. He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1925–1940) and Kanazawa University (~1940–1941).

R. H. Tawney (1880–1962) was a historian educated at Rugby School and Balliol College, Oxford. He held academic posts at the University of Glasgow (~1906–1908) and the London School of Economics (~1917–1949).

R. K. Bodhe completed a Master of Pharmacy at R.C. Patel Institute (2017–2019) and served as Research Officer at the Kaivalyadhama Health and Yoga Research Center (attested 2005), working in Indology and other fields.
A scholar in Japanology and religious studies, Kimbrough earned his PhD at Yale University. He held an academic post at the University of Colorado Boulder (attested 2013).
R. N. Gadre was an Indology scholar who served as Professor of Sanskrit at Sir Parashurambhau College and at Savitribai Phule Pune University, both attested in 1958.
R. P. Paranjpye (1876–1966) studied under Vaman Shivram Apte and served as Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (attested 1959).
A scholar of philosophy and Indology, R. Ramanujachari was Professor of Philosophy at Annamalai University (attested 1938–1940) and editor of the Journal of the Annamalai University (attested 1950).
